## Summary

Built the five Chronicle core navigation modules under `design/visual-lab/src/core/`, all pure TypeScript with no React/DOM dependency on the app:

- **`scope.ts`** — platform/universe/campaign/session path parsing, prefix-consuming, `formatScope(parseScope(p)) === p` round-trips.
- **`objectRef.ts`** — canonical `type:id@revision` text form (never the slug), `sameObject` compares type+id+scope but ignores revision.
- **`viewRecipe.ts`** — the exact §4.3 mapping table (character/scene/article/place × workspace), no `Role` concept at all per spec.
- **`visibility.ts`** — the sharpest one: `secret` always returns `not_found` (never `redacted`) for non-GM roles, so a locked-row render can't confirm a secret's existence; `open` returns `not_found` for `public` since campaign content isn't public.
- **`deepLink.ts`** — builds/parses the four URL shapes from §6.5 using the real `URL`/`URLSearchParams` APIs for correct percent-encoding round trips.

Two judgment calls worth flagging:
1. Couldn't use the `.ts`-suffixed imports shown in the brief's own code blocks — `tsconfig.json` (which I'm barred from touching) doesn't have `allowImportingTsExtensions`, so imports are extension-less.
2. `deepLink.ts` unifies the doc's two different object-embedding styles (bare slug in path for `world`, `scene=`/`recipe=` query keys for `table`) into one consistent `/objects/<type:id@revision>` path segment — a generic encoder can't derive a workspace-specific query key like `"scene"`, and a bare slug alone can't round-trip full `ObjectRef` identity. Documented inline in the file.

Verified with a throwaway smoke script (not committed) exercising round-trips, GM-tier/visibility matrix, and recipe survival — all matched expected values — then confirmed `npm --prefix design/visual-lab run build` passes clean.
